marketAlerts.text: CMA CGM eBusiness was inside a scheduled maintenance window (Sat 12 Sep 17:00 CEST to Sun 13 Sep 05:00 CEST) for the whole run. The routing-finder POST that PART A relies on returned the bare page shell with zero sailings on all four probe lanes, and the GET page carried the maintenance banner. Fell through to fallback (2) COSCO e-lines. Discovered COSCO exposes a clean same-origin JSON endpoint, POST /ebschedule/public/purpoShipmentWs, that needs no autocomplete interaction: body is fromDate/toDate/originCityUuid/destinationCityUuid/originCity/destinationCity/cargoNature, city ids come from /ebbase/public/general/findCityByPrefix. All 19 Ocean Alliance lanes returned 200 with no rate limiting.

Premier no longer needs the ONE Route Finder UI. The results page calls GET https://ecomm.one-line.com/api/v1/schedule/point-to-point with porCode/delCode/rcvTermCode/deTermCode/fromDate/toDate/cargoNature/searchType, which returns every sailing as JSON with no 10-row page cap and no throttle modal. Twenty-seven lanes ran in one session against the PART C limit of about three. The call is CORS-blocked from www.one-line.com, so the tab must sit on the ecomm.one-line.com origin. Cai Mep resolves under VNSGN, not VNCMT or VNVUT, which both still return zero.

Flexport Atlas same-origin fetch worked this run. The PART E warning that /vessel/name:<slug> hangs from an Atlas page did not reproduce, so 45 vessels were verified by fetch instead of one tab navigation each. Atlas does strip the URL hash on its SPA redirect, so the cross-origin hash funnel cannot be used to hand a work list into an Atlas tab.

Five ports carried forward because this run had no fresh source for them. Gemini TP11 Haiphong (Maersk returns 422 on all three Haiphong lanes, unchanged from 12 Sep). Ocean Alliance ECC1 Kaohsiung and GCC1 Shekou (neither is in the COSCO lane set that replaced the blocked CMA source). Premier EC3 Busan and EC3 Ningbo (the ONE API returned EC1 but no EC3 on those two lanes to New York). Everything else is fresh.

Eighteen week-level backfills applied, all of them early-window. Every external source was queried from 13 Sep, so week 37 departures dated 07 to 12 Sep can only come from the previous run. Affected: ECC1 Yantian/Hong Kong/Port Klang, ECX1 Laem Chabang/Hong Kong/Xiamen/Shanghai, GCC1 Shanghai/Busan, GCC2 Ningbo, EC3 Tianjin/Qingdao/Cai Mep, EC4 Cai Mep, TP11 Busan, AMBERJACK Qingdao/Ningbo, EMERALD Xiamen.

WAN HAI 712 corrected from 7000 to 7092 TEU against Flexport Atlas (IMO 9965332). The same value was written into market_prev.json so the notify email does not report it as a day-over-day capacity change. Three vessels new to the cache: EVER LEGION 8452, HYUNDAI JUPITER 10055, MSC QINGDAO 8667. Forty-six vessels now carry an Atlas asOf of 13 Sep 2026.

Both known extra loaders still running, neither changed. WHL+HPL AA9: WAN HAI 903 (8700 TEU), Port Klang 30 Sep, Cai Mep 05 Oct, Shekou 11 Oct, Ningbo 15 Oct, Qingdao 19 Oct, via Balboa to New York 23 Nov, about one day slower than AA7 proforma on the shared pairs. Gemini XL: MAERSK MONTANA (4544 TEU) voy 639E, Yantian 23 Sep and Busan 28 Sep to Houston 31 Oct, roughly five days slower than TP15. No new non-proforma service codes surfaced on any US East Coast or Gulf discharge this run.

Proforma coverage 21 of 21 services, but five entries carry a null asOf and should be re-pulled when there is budget: Gemini TP11/TP12/TP15/TP16 have no published per-lane transit table located, and ZIM EMPIRE/AMERICA/LONE STAR still need a dated pull from zim.com point-to-point. Ocean Alliance (31 Aug) and Premier (08 Sep) are inside the 30-day window and were deliberately not re-fetched. AA7 re-derived today as a median off the long-term CSV and marked derived.

No additions, terminations or rotation changes. All seven Ocean Alliance codes returned (AWE1/AWE2/AWE3/AWE4/AWE7/GME/GME2), all four Gemini TP strings, all four Premier EC strings, all five ZIM+MSC services and AA7. MS2 stays absent from the profile and MS2 rows were dropped at parse time, as were FP2 and the other deny-listed codes.

Cut-off strings from the two new sources arrived in their native formats - COSCO returns 2026-09-17 12:00 and MSC returns Sat 29th Aug 2026 08:00 - instead of the DD Mon hh:mm the cell spec requires. All affected cells were normalised in a follow-up commit so the CY column reads consistently across carried-forward and freshly-scraped sailings.
